messages:
liam (Partnerships): FYI vendor flagged intermittent node reboots on H200 blades in eu-west-1 during sustained multi-tenant runs. They think it's power sequencing + firmware interaction. Asking if we want to open an embargoed joint bulletin or quietly shift marketplace traffic.

nina (Sales Ops): This is visible in customer queue: 4 enterprise customers have reserved H200 capacity next week. We need a commercial note if we change their slots. Prefer quiet swap if possible.

rohan (Eng-ML): From model side, H200 behavior looks fine until mix of long-context + high concurrency >120 req/s. We see kernel OOMs then watchdog reboots. Logs attached by vendor show: 
```
[WARN] nvlink: reset triggered
[ERROR] firmware: power_seq_timeout
[INFO] watchdog: pid 4321 killed
```

tara (Infrastructure): Ops options: (A) Route eu-west H200 -> eu-west H100 if latency-tolerant, (B) Route -> mi300 instances (cross-zone), or (C) enforce concurrency caps per tenant. I prefer C + B as primary.

kevin (Partner Eng): I'll ask vendor for root cause ETA. Also confirming whether BMC firmware patch is ready. If patch >48h, we should enact routing plan.

liam (Partnerships): Quick decision needed: do we notify press/legal now? Legal: potential joint press only if vendor requests embargo. Otherwise keep internal.

nina (Sales Ops): Sales ask: if we move a reserved slot, can we guarantee same price? If not, need immediate customer outreach. I can prepare template offering temporary credit.

rohan (Eng-ML): Proposed temporary runtime knobs: 
- per-tenant concurrency cap: 80req/s on /models/redwood/h200
- reduce max batch to 6 for h200 routes
- fallback precedence: mi300 (same region) > h100 (lower cost)
Implement as router policy change + quota rule.

tara (Infrastructure): I'll add two monitoring rules: node_reboot_count >3 per rack in 30m and firmware_errors >0. Also creating a runbook step: quarantine rack and failover if reboot_count >=5.

kevin (Partner Eng): Vendor replied: BMC firmware v1.2.4 patch available but requires maintenance window and cold reboot. They offered canary on 2 racks tomorrow at 02:00 UTC. Patch ETA 36h for general availability.

liam (Partnerships): Ok timeline: enforce runtime caps now, do canary patch tomorrow 02:00 UTC, full rollout after vendor validation. We won't do a press joint announce unless vendor requests.

nina (Sales Ops): Drafting customer message: short, apologetic, list of options (credit, keep reserved but moved to mi300, opt-out). Draft ETA 30m.

rohan (Eng-ML): Router snippet to flip on: 
```
routing:
 - match: "/models/redwood/h200"
   concurrency_cap: 80
   max_batch: 6
   fallbacks: ["/models/redwood/mi300-eu","/models/redwood/h100-eu"]
   billing_notice: "fallback_cost_delta"
```
I'll open PR.

tara (Infrastructure): I'll schedule the quarantine playbook and set the alert dashboards. Also adding a short SSH checklist for on-call to capture dmesg and BMC logs: 
- ssh root@rack-node
- sudo journalctl -u vendor-bmc -n 500
- sudo dmesg | tail -n 200

kevin (Partner Eng): Confirmed vendor asks for embargoed window only if we publish joint advisory. They prefer we internally handle failover and push patch quietly.

liam (Partnerships): Decision thread summary: action owners -> Rohan: router PR (10m), Tara: alerts + runbook (20m), Nina: customer comms draft (30m), Kevin: vendor canary coord (36h patch window). We'll revisit after PR + comms. If any customer escalates, escalate to me and legal.

comms-bot: scheduled-message: Reminder: post updates to #support and #eng-oncall after changes.

nina (Sales Ops): ack, posting draft to this thread in 20m for quick review.

rohan (Eng-ML): PR created: runtime/h200-fallbacks (#512). Includes tests for concurrency cap enforcement. Requesting review from @tara and @kevin.

liam (Partnerships): Thanks team. If vendor flips canary tomorrow, we may need a 01:30 UTC quick win-room. I'll create cal invite if needed. :calendar:
